operational-example.copy: Use Empty State when a surface has no useful content yet and the user needs context, next action, or recovery.

rationale: Empty State explains absence instead of leaving a blank surface.
The ZIP reference uses a centered column, 64px muted icon circle, compact title, restrained description, and optional action.
Use it for recoverable absence, not as a replacement for loading, error detail, or marketing copy.

items.rule: Centers the absence message inside the owning surface.
Provides a quiet visual anchor without competing with primary actions.
Names the absence in human language.
Explains cause, expectation, or recovery in one short sentence.
Optional direct recovery when the user can act now.

accessibility.statePrecedence: error, loading, permission, action, search-empty, default
items: Use visible text for the absence; do not rely on icon meaning.
Only render an action when it is available and useful.
Keep the title and description close to the empty surface.
Do not announce decorative icons as content.
Use Inline Validation or Toast when the absence is caused by a recent user action.

variants.copy: Empty State variants describe the reason for absence: first use, search empty, permission, error, and maintenance.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Empty State as absence recovery: agents can draft the reason and next action, while humans confirm cause, permission, and business consequence.
canDecide: Use for empty lists, panels, dashboards, and search results.
Use one recovery action when the next step is clear.
Keep absence copy short and specific.
mustAsk: The absence may be caused by permissions, outage, or data delay.
The recovery action changes data or access.
The empty surface could be loading instead.
rejectIf: The state hides an actual error or permission issue.
miel.handoff: I am using Empty State because the surface has no content. Please confirm the cause, recovery action, and whether this is absence, loading, permission, or error.
